newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: PALM OIL - Southeast Asian prices seen in range.
newsitem.headline: PALM OIL - Southeast Asian prices seen in range.

text.p: Malaysian palm oil prices are expected to trade sideways this week while prices in Indonesia are seen steady on continued fresh buying and adjustment to crude palm oil prices, regional traders said.
They said prices in Malaysia were likely to be locked in tight ranges as the market looks for fresh direction.

"The market appears to be well supported. But we don't think prices can go up much as there are also many players looking for levels to sell," said a Malaysian trader. He said a softening in exports would keep a lid on prices.
Cargo surveyor Societe Generale de Surveillance (SGS) estimated Malaysia's palm oil exports for November 1-15 at 298,862 tonnes compared with 374,988 tonnes for October 1-15.
Traders said a shortage in ships to transport the oil may also introduce a downward tilt in the market.

"Most of the focus will be on the lack of ships to transport the oil. There's a whole queue of people looking for ships. Anyone who's got freight is king," said the managing director of a Singapore-based vegetable oil trading company.
But another trader in a Western commodity house said the tightness in ships "is seasonal" and the market may trend sideways in the meantime.
"It will still be in a range," a dealer said, adding prices of the third position contract will likely move "between 1,150 to 1,220 ringgit".
Third position January crude palm oil futures contract closed at 1,194 ringgit a tonne on Friday.
October crop figures released by the Palm Oil Registration and Licensing Authority (PORLA) on Friday were quickly discounted by the market since they were within traders' expectations.
"The numbers were seen as neutral," one trader said.

PORLA put Malaysia's end-October palm oil stocks at 953,241 tonnes, up from 894,438 at end-September. Output in October was 883,579 tonnes, against 864,730 in September, and exports were 727,629 tonnes versus September's 649,688, PORLA said.
Although prices in Indonesia were expected to hold firm, traders said the upside could be limited.
"I think there will be continued support (this) week, but I don't see the market surging like it did (last) week," one said. "There could be some consolidation towards end of the week."
Local olein prices climbed to 1,415 rupiah/kg in Jakarta on Friday from 1,360-70 rupiah a week earlier following a sharp increase in crude palm oil prices.
Crude palm oil topped 1,215 rupiah/kg in the North Sumatran city of Medan on Friday against 1,195 rupiah/kg the previous week.
"I think olein prices (in Jakarta) could rise by 10 to 20 rupiah next week because at the moment, there is very little margin in processing crude palm oil into olein," one said.
(With contributions from K.T. Arasu in Jakarta and Rene Pastor in Singapore)
